```{r}
#| include: FALSE
#| warnings: FALSE
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(tidyverse)
    library(fs)
    library(gt)
    library(here)
    library(patchwork)

    library(ggh4x)

```


The start of chromosome 2 shows low divergence in the  *H. elegans*  - *H. major*
comparison, even after masking putatively misassembled regions. This region is
known to house many V2R genes (Li et al. 2021).

Here we overlay the divergence signals with V2R annotations on the *H. major*
genome. We then show the number of V2R genes in other snakes as a general comparison.

## V2R annotation pipeline (in brief)

The scripts for obtaining potential V2R genes are in the [scripts][scripts]
directory. Annotating V2Rs is tricky, as they often exist in large clusters meaning
gene prediction tools have trouble. Instead, we use the approach from Li et al.
(2021) where we use the presence of 7-transmembrane domains (7tm) as evidence of
a V2R gene. 

The pipeline we developed is broken into two phases; Protein alignment to obtain
gene regions and 7tm annotation and curation.

### Step 1: Protein alignment

V2R protein sequences were downloaded from NCBI NR, Swiss-Prot and TrEMBL
databases.

Headers were simplified - e.g. from `>tr|A0A1S3WWH9|A0A1S3WWH9_ERIEU`
to `V2R:A0A1S3WWH9` - and merged from each source  into a single file. Representative
sequences were obtained using `mmseqs easy-cluster`. Parameters from the `mmseqs2` 
[user-guide][ec] were followed to ensure short fragments weren't used as
representative sequences.

To help parameterise `miniprot` alignment, we obtained V2R intron sizes by extracting
V2R sequences from *P. textilis*, *N. scutatus*, *P. mucrosquamatus*, *C. adamanteus*
and *T. elegans*, which all have RefSeq gene annotations.

```{r intron sizes}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 150
#| warnings: FALSE
intron_dists <- dir_ls(
    here("results", "05-v2r", "intron-length-dist"),
    glob = "*introns.gff3"
) |>
    read_tsv(
        comment = "#",
        col_names = FALSE,
        id = "species",
        col_types = cols()
    ) |>
    filter(X3 == "intron") |>
    select(species, start = X4, end = X5, gene = X9) |>
    mutate(
        species = sub(".+/intron-length-dist/(.*)-v2r.+", "\\1", species),
        gene = case_when(
            species == "crotalus_adamanteus" ~ sub(
                ".+locus_tag=(.*);orig_protein_id.+",
                "\\1",
                gene
            ),
            species == "thamnophis_elegans" ~ sub(
                ".+gene=(.*);product.+",
                "\\1",
                gene
            ),
            .default = sub(".+gene=(.*);product.*", "\\1", gene)
        ),
        length = abs(end - start),
        mean_species = mean(length),
        median_species = median(length),
        .by = species
    ) |>
    mutate(
        mean_species_gene = mean(length),
        median_species_gene = median(length),
        .by = c(species, gene)
    )

intron_dists |>
    ggplot(aes(x = length, fill = species, colour = species)) +
    geom_step(
        stat = "bin",
        bins = 50,
        direction = "mid"
    ) +
    geom_histogram(
        bins = 50,
        position = "identity",
        alpha = 0.3,
        colour = NA
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 10), expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = paletteer::paletteer_d("PNWColors::Bay")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = paletteer::paletteer_d("PNWColors::Bay")) +
    annotation_logticks(sides = 'b', outside = TRUE) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
    labs(x = "\nLength (bp)") +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2), colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
    theme_linedraw() +
    theme(
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.text.x = element_text(vjust = -2),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom"
    )
```

Intron-size peaks around 1-2kbp in length. If we look at the 20 longest introns,
we can see that there are some massive ones (>100kbp), but there is a jump from
30-40Kbp mark to the higher values. Consequently, we used a value of 45,000bp as
our max-intron size when aligning the proteins.

```{r}
intron_dists |> 
    arrange(desc(length)) |> 
    print(n = 20)
```

Protein alignments were manually curated to split chimeric alignments.
Curated alignments were then formatted with `AGAT` before "gene" loci were 
merged if they overlapped using `bedtools merge`, resulting in **putative V2R**
**gene loci**. 

The issue is these numbers are much lower than expected, likely due to:

- sequence complexity at the start of chromosome 2
- mapping divergent protein sequences

As such, we used these proteins as a first pass, and used the features (7tm) in
these alignments for additional curation.

### Step 2: 7tm annotation

V2R sequences were extracted from the *H. major* reference genome using the V2R
`miniprot` alignments above. These sequences were then searched against `Pfam`
to annotate functional domains using `hmmerscan`. The `.domtblout` file was then
filtered using the following criteria:

- c-evalue $\leq1e^{-5}$
- The length of the alignment must match the length of the Pfam target

The sequences were extracted using `bedtools getfasta`, before being clustered
into representative sequences using `CD-HIT`.

With the curated candidate sequences, we then searched the genomes of the other
sea snakes six snakes using `TBLASTN`.

`TBLASTN` hits were then filtered using the code below.

```{r filter tblastn}
#| warnings: FALSE
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 150
cnames <- c(
    "qseqid",
    "sseqid",
    "pident",
    "length",
    "mismatch",
    "gapopen",
    "qstart",
    "qend",
    "sstart",
    "send",
    "evalue",
    "bitscore"
)

# Chromosome renaming
rename_hcy <- read_tsv(
    here("data", "HCY-seq-report.tsv"),
    col_types = cols()
) |>
    select(sseqid = `GenBank seq accession`, chrom = `Chromosome name`) |>
    filter(str_starts(sseqid, "CM")) |>
    mutate(chrom = paste0("chr", chrom))

rename_hcu_ncbi <- read_tsv(
    here("data", "HCU-NCBI-seq-report.tsv"),
    col_types = cols()
) |>
    select(sseqid = `GenBank seq accession`, chrom = `Chromosome name`) |>
    filter(str_starts(sseqid, "CM")) |>
    mutate(chrom = paste0("chr", chrom))

# Ordering
chrs <- c(paste0("chr", 1:18), "chrZ")
forder <- c("HMA", "HOR", "HEL", "HCU-UAE", "HCU-NCBI", "HCY")

# Filters: alignment length == query length, alignment >= 200aa, e-value <= 1e-10
df_tblastn <- fs::dir_ls(
    here("results", "05-v2r", "tblastn-7tm"),
    glob = "*outfmt6"
) |>
    read_tsv(
        col_names = cnames,
        col_types = cols(),
        id = "file"
    ) |>
    mutate(file = str_remove(basename(file), ".7tm.*")) |>
    left_join(bind_rows(rename_hcy, rename_hcu_ncbi)) |>
    mutate(
        sseqid = ifelse(is.na(chrom), sseqid, chrom),
        sseqid = factor(sseqid, levels = chrs),
        species = case_when(
            file == "HCU-NCBI" ~ "H. curtus (East)",
            file == "HCU-UAE" ~ "H. curtus (West)",
            file == "HCY" ~ "H. cyanocinctus",
            file == "HEL" ~ "H. elegans",
            file == "HMA" ~ "H. major",
            file == "HOR" ~ "H. ornatus"
        ),
        file = factor(file, forder)
    ) |>
    select(-chrom)

# Length distribution before filtering
df_tblastn |>
    ggplot(aes(x = length, fill = species)) +
    geom_step(
        aes(colour = species),
        stat = "bin",
        bins = 50,
        direction = "mid"
    ) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50, alpha = 0.5, position = "identity") +
    scale_y_continuous(
        name = "Count (K)",
        breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 6), 
        labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-3),
        expand = c(0.01, 0)
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5), expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
    facet_wrap(vars(file), ncol = 2) +
    labs(x = "Length (bp)") +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
    theme_linedraw() +
    theme(
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom"
    )
```

We can see that most alignments are $\geq$ 200aa in length, so we filter
anything out less than this. This also fits with most 7tm domains that were predicted
having lengths ~250aa, which is where we see the biggest peak in all datasets.

Next, we visualise the percentage-identity (pid) distribution. At this point,
there are a lot of redundant features still in the table (i.e. different query
sequences aligning to the same locus). Here, we're just trying to see what a
reasonable pid-threshold would be.

Evidently, it's around 60%, as there is a peak there, and almost all the data
resides to the right of this mark.

```{r}
#| warnings: FALSE
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| dpi: 150
df_tblastn <- df_tblastn |>
    filter(qstart == 1, qend == length, length >= 200, evalue <= 1e-10) |>
    arrange(file, sseqid, sstart, desc(bitscore))

# NOTE: there are many redundant hits to putative loci in this figure. The goal
# is to get an idea of what the pid distribution looks like to inform filtering.
# The peak at 60 and 70(-ish) will have counts higher than the final collapsed
# version
df_tblastn |>
    ggplot(aes(x = pident, fill = species)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 60, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_step(
        aes(colour = species),
        stat = "bin",
        bins = 50,
        direction = "mid"
    ) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50, alpha = 0.5, position = "identity") +
    scale_y_continuous(
        name = "Count (K)",
        breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 6), 
        labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-3),
        expand = c(0.01, 0)
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
        name = "% identity", 
        limits = c(0, 100),
        breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 10), 
        expand = c(0.01, 0)
    ) +
    facet_wrap(vars(file), ncol = 2) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
    theme_linedraw() +
    theme(
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.background.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom"
    )
```

With that in mind, we apply the %-ID filter and export the valid co-ordinates.
There are going to be many redundant hits which will be filtered out in the next
step.

```{r}
#| warnings: FALSE
# Writing the curated TBLASTN hits to BED files
df_tblastn |>
    filter(pident >= 60) |>
    mutate(
        start = ifelse(sstart > send, send, sstart),
        end = ifelse(sstart > send, sstart, send)
    ) |>
    select(file, sseqid, start, end) |>
    arrange(file, sseqid, start) |>
    (\(x) split(x, x$file))() |>
    iwalk(\(x, i) {
        # If sample is Hcy/Hcu - fix chromosome names back to NCBI version
        if (i == "HCY") {
            x <- x |>
                left_join(rename_hcy, by = join_by(sseqid == chrom)) |>
                select(file, sseqid = sseqid.y, start, end)
        } else if (i == "HCU-NCBI") {
            x <- x |>
                left_join(rename_hcu_ncbi, by = join_by(sseqid == chrom)) |>
                select(file, sseqid = sseqid.y, start, end)
        }
        x |>
            select(-file) |>
            write_tsv(
                file = glue::glue(
                    here(
                        "results",
                        "05-v2r",
                        "tblastn-7tm",
                        "{i}-7tm.candidates.bed"
                    )
                ),
                col_names = FALSE
            )
    })
```

The command `bedtools merge` was then used to collapse overlapping 7tm domains,
reducing the redundancy massively, and giving us our final V2R proxy set.

## V2R gene content

Now we're interested in actually exploring V2R content in snakes. We'll overlay
the divergence estimates for the three sea snakes along the *H. major* genome,
along with the *H. major* V2R annotations.

Then we'll explore V2R content in a range of other snakes. Note that we aren't
performing manual curation of chromosome 2 where the V2Rs exist in the other
snakes, so there is very likely going to be some misassembly. The numbers should
be considered as a snapshot of V2R content as the genomes exist today.

```{r}
#| warnings: FALSE
# Colour palettes
pal_between <- c(
    "HCU-HEL" = "#09283CFF",
    "HCU-HMA" = "#F2EBBBFF",
    "HEL-HMA" = "#F18B00FF"
)

pal_within <- c("HMA" = "#fca311", "HCU" = "#59A14FFF", "HEL" = "#4E79A7FF")

pal_long <- c(
    "HCU-HEL" = "#09283CFF",
    "HCU-HMA" = "#F2EBBBFF",
    "HEL-HMA" = "#F18B00FF",
    "HMA" = "#fca311", 
    "HCU" = "#59A14FFF", 
    "HEL" = "#4E79A7FF"
)

# Partial figure 4
fig_4_partial <- read_rds(here("manuscript", "figures", "figure-4-partial.rds"))

# Mask regions
gr_mask <- read_csv(
    here("results", "05-v2r", "hifi-coverage", "mask-regions.csv"),
    col_types = cols()
) |>
    select(chrom, start = xmin, end = xmax) |>
    GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame()

# Already filtered for mis-assembly
df_fst_dxy <- read_csv(
    here("results", "03-diversity", "between", "clean-data.csv"),
    col_types = cols()
) |>
    mutate(chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = 1:16))

df_pi <- read_csv(
    here(
        "results",
        "03-diversity",
        "within",
        "ref-hmaj",
        "clean-data.csv"
    ),
    col_types = cols()
) |>
    mutate(chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = 1:16))

df_7tm <- read_tsv(
    here(
        "results",
        "05-v2r",
        "tblastn-7tm",
        "HMA-7tm.candidates.merged.bed"
    ),
    col_names = c("chrom", "start", "end"),
    col_types = cols()
)
```

### 7tm's in problematic regions

First thing we do is identify which 7tm (V2Rs) overlap problematic regions. A total
of 123 7tm sequences overlap the mask-regions. These genes may belong to the Z
chromosome, or simply exist in hard to assemble chomosome 2 sequence.

As such, I've elected to not add them to either chromosome, instead leaving them
as their own category.

```{r}
overlaps <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(
    df_7tm |> GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(keep.extra.columns = TRUE),
    gr_mask
)

df_7tm$overlaps_mask <- FALSE
df_7tm$overlaps_mask[S4Vectors::queryHits(overlaps)] <- TRUE

df_7tm <- df_7tm |>
    mutate(
        chrom = ifelse(overlaps_mask, "mask region", chrom),
        type = "CDS", 
        strand = "+"
    )

df_7tm |>
    summarise("7tm_count" = n(), .by = chrom)
```

### Divergence signal *H. major*

Now that we've masked genes that exist in the problematic regions of chromosome 2,
we can go an build the figure for the manuscript.

```{r}
#| warnings: FALSE
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 12
#| dpi: 300
# Gene track
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(gggenomes)})
fai <- read_tsv(
    here("data", "genomes", "HMA.fa.fai"), 
    c("chrom", "length"), 
    col_types = cols(), 
    col_select = c(chrom, length)
) |>
    filter(chrom == "chr2") |>
    mutate(seq_id = "H. major")

tmp <- df_7tm |> 
    filter(chrom == "chr2", !overlaps_mask) |>
    mutate(seq_id = "H. major", feature = "7TM domain") 

p_track <- gggenomes(
    seqs = fai,
    genes = tmp
) +
    geom_seq(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_gene(
        aes(fill = feature, colour = feature),
        rna_aes=aes(fill = fill, colour=colour),
        size = 6,
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("#415a77", "#fcbf49")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#415a77", "#fcbf49")) +
    scale_x_continuous(
        name = "Chromosome 2 (Mb)",
        labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6),
        breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 10),
        expand = c(0,0)
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
        axis.line.x = element_line(size = 0.5),
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),,
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
        plot.margin = grid::unit(c(0, 0, 5, 0), "mm")
    )

# Divergence track
between_long <- df_fst_dxy |>
    pivot_longer(names_to = "statistic", values_to = "values", c(zfst, avg_dxy)) |>
    select(comparison, chromosome, window_pos_1, window_pos_2, statistic, values)

within_long <- df_pi |>
    pivot_longer(names_to = "statistic", values_to = "values", avg_pi) |>
    rename(comparison = pop) |>
    select(comparison, chromosome, window_pos_1, window_pos_2, statistic, values)

data_long <- bind_rows(between_long, within_long) |>
    mutate(
        statistic = replace_when(
            statistic,
            statistic == "zfst" ~ "*ZF~ST~*",
            statistic == "avg_dxy" ~ "*d~XY~*",
            statistic == "avg_pi" ~ "*π*"
        ),
        statistic = forcats::fct_inorder(statistic)
    )

p_div <- data_long |>
    filter(chromosome == 2) |>
    ggplot(
        aes(
            x = floor((window_pos_1 + window_pos_2)/ 2), 
            y = values, 
            colour = comparison
        )
    ) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.05) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.1, alpha = 0.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(
        name = "Position (Mb)",
        labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6),
        breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 10),
        expand = c(0,0)
    ) +
    facet_grid(
        vars(statistic),
        scales = "free_y",
        switch = "y",
    ) +
    ggh4x::facetted_pos_scales( y = list(
        statistic == "ZF~ST~" ~ scale_y_continuous(
            breaks = c(-3, 0, 3),
            labels = c("-3", "0", "3"),
            limits = c(-5, 3.5)
        ),
        statistic == "d~XY~" ~ scale_y_continuous(
            breaks = c(0, 0.005, 0.01, 0.015),
            labels = c("0", "0.005", "0.01", "0.015"),
            limits = c(0, 0.015)
        ),
        statistic == "π" ~ scale_y_continuous(
            breaks = c(0, 0.0025, 0.005, 0.0075),
            labels = c("0", "0.0025", "0.005", "0.0075"),
            limits = c(0, 0.01)
        ))
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal_long) +
    labs(tag = "D") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y.left = element_markdown(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        plot.tag = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
        plot.margin = grid::unit(c(0, 0, 5, 0), "mm")
    )

# Plot layout
design <- "
AAAAAAABBB
AAAAAAABBB
CCCCCCCDDD
CCCCCCCDDD
CCCCCCCDDD
CCCCCCCDDD
CCCCCCCDDD
CCCCCCCDDD
EEEEEEEEEE
EEEEEEEEEE
EEEEEEEEEE
EEEEEEEEEE
FFFFFFFFFF
"

figure_4 <- wrap_plots(
    A = fig_4_partial$A,
    B = guide_area(),
    C = fig_4_partial$B,
    D = fig_4_partial$C,
    E = p_div,

) +
    plot_layout(design = design, guides = "collect") &
    guides(
        colour = guide_legend(

        )
    ) &
    theme(
        legend.position = "none",
        # legend.box = "vertical",

        # legend.title.position = "top"
    )

# The legend of this figure is edited in Adobe Illustrator
cairo_pdf(
    filename = here(
        "manuscript",

        "figure-4_genome-scan.pdf"
    ),
    width = 14,
    height = 16,
)
figure_4
invisible(dev.off())
figure_4
```

### Supplementary: V2Rs (7TM) in other snakes

Lastly, we'll look at V2R content in other snakes that have chromosome scale genomes.
This is not an exhaustive list, but provides a good overview of what V2R dynamics
look like.

```{r v2r-total}
#| warnings: FALSE
terrestrial_v2r_total <- dir_ls(here("data"), glob = "*-gene-ids.txt") |>
    map(read_lines) |>
    map_vec(length) |>
    (\(x) tibble(id = str_remove(basename(names(x)), "-.*"), Total = x))() |>
    mutate(
        id = ifelse(id == "CAD", "C. adamanteus", "T. elegans"),
        type = "V2R"
    )

marine_7tm_total <- fs::dir_ls(path = here("results", "05-v2r", "tblastn-7tm"), glob = "*merged*") |>
    map_vec(\(x) read_tsv(x, col_names = FALSE, col_types = cols()) |> nrow()) |>
    (\(x) tibble(id = str_remove(basename(names(x)), "-7tm.*"), Total = x))() |>
    mutate(
        id = case_when(
            id == "HCU-NCBI" ~ "H. curtus (East)",
            id == "HCU-UAE" ~ "H. curtus (West)",
            id == "HCY" ~ "H. cyanocinctus",
            id == "HEL" ~ "H. elegans",
            id == "HMA" ~ "H. major",
            id == "HOR" ~ "H. ornatus"
        ),
        type = "7TM"
    )

bind_rows(terrestrial_v2r_total, marine_7tm_total) |>
    write_csv(here("manuscript", "tables", "supplementary", "supp-total-V2R-7tm.csv"))

bind_rows(terrestrial_v2r_total, marine_7tm_total)
```

We can also see how V2Rs exist along the chromosomes in each snake.

> NOTE: I'm not applying the chromsome 2 correction to *H. major* here.

```{r}
#| warnings: FALSE
# Chromosome IDs
seq_reports <- c(
    "CAD" = here("data", "CAD-seq-report.tsv"), 
    "TEL" = here("data", "TEL-seq-report.tsv"),
    "HCU-NCBI" = here("data", "HCU-NCBI-seq-report.tsv"),
    "HCY" = here("data", "HCY-seq-report.tsv")
) |>
    imap(\(x, i) {
        if(i %in% c("CAD", "HCU-NCBI", "HCY")) {
            x |> 
                read_tsv(col_types = cols()) |>
                select(X1 = `GenBank seq accession`, chrom = `Chromosome name`)
        } else {
            x |> 
                read_tsv(col_types = cols()) |>
                select(X1 = `RefSeq seq accession`, chrom = `Chromosome name`)
        }
    })

terrestrial_v2r_gene_ids <- fs::dir_ls(here("data"), glob = "*-gene-ids.txt") |>
    (\(x) set_names(x, str_remove(basename(names(x)), "-.*")))() |>
    map(read_lines)

terrestrial_v2r_count_chrom <- fs::dir_ls(here("data"), glob = "*gff") |>
    (\(x) x[str_detect(x, "HMA", negate = TRUE)])() |>
    (\(x) set_names(x, str_remove(basename(names(x)), ".gff")))() |>
    map(read_tsv, col_names = FALSE, col_types = cols(), comment = "#") |>
    imap(\(x, i) {
        x |>
            filter(X3 == "gene") |>
            mutate(X9 = str_remove(X9, ";.*"), X9 = str_remove(X9, "ID=")) |>
            filter(X9 %in% terrestrial_v2r_gene_ids[[i]]) |>
            left_join(seq_reports[[i]])
    }) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "id") |>
    summarise(count = n(), .by = c(id, chrom)) |>
    mutate(
        chrom = paste0("chr", chrom),
        type = "V2R",
        id = ifelse(id == "CAD", "C. adamanteus", "T. elegans"),
    )

# Marine 7TM
marine_v2r_count_chrom <- fs::dir_ls(path = here("results", "05-v2r", "tblastn-7tm"), glob = "*merged*") |>
    map(\(x) read_tsv(x, col_names = FALSE, col_types = cols())) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "id") |>
    mutate(id = str_remove(basename(id), "-7tm.*")) |>
    summarise(count = n(), .by = c(id, X1)) |>
    left_join(seq_reports |> list_rbind()) |>
    mutate(
        chrom = ifelse(!is.na(chrom), paste0("chr", chrom), chrom),
        chrom = ifelse(is.na(chrom), X1, chrom),
        id = case_when(
            id == "HCU-NCBI" ~ "H. curtus (East)",
            id == "HCU-UAE" ~ "H. curtus (West)",
            id == "HCY" ~ "H. cyanocinctus",
            id == "HEL" ~ "H. elegans",
            id == "HMA" ~ "H. major",
            id == "HOR" ~ "H. ornatus"
        ),
        type = "7TM"
    ) |>
    select(-X1)

v2r_7tm_chrom <- bind_rows(marine_v2r_count_chrom, terrestrial_v2r_count_chrom) |>
    mutate(
        chrom = factor(
            chrom, 
            levels = c(paste0("chr", 1:18), "chrZ", "chrW", "chrUn")
        )
    ) |>
    arrange(chrom) |>
    select(-type) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = id, values_from = count)

v2r_7tm_chrom |>
    write_csv(here("manuscript", "tables", "supplementary", "supp-V2R-7tm-by-chrom.csv"), na = "")

v2r_7tm_chrom

v2r_7tm_chrom |>
  gt(rowname_col = "chrom") |>
  fmt_number(columns = everything(), use_seps = TRUE, decimals = 0) |>
  sub_missing(missing_text = "-") |>
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = everything()) |>
  cols_label(
    `H. curtus (East)` = md("*H. curtus* (East)"),
    `H. curtus (West)` = md("*H. curtus* (West)"),
    `H. cyanocinctus` = md("*H. cyanocinctus*"),
    `H. elegans` = md("*H. elegans*"),
    `H. major` = md("*H. major*"),
    `H. ornatus` = md("*H. ornatus*"),
    `C. adamanteus` = md("*C. adamanteus*"),
    `T. elegans` = md("*T. elegans*")
  ) |>
  tab_stubhead(label = "Chromosome") |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) |>
  as_raw_html()
```
